_comment: Diagnostic only: stride 1 so closing inflation can be separated from the reconstruction of pixels that striding discards. The GRAND control (grand_colca_stride1.json) measured striding unbiased at a 1 km closing element; this is the same test at TAMBO's 100 m element, where the run's own funnel reports a closing factor below 1 and the area is therefore a lower bound. Not a config to keep.
_comment_slope: Colca's walls are ~40 deg, far outside GRAND's 3-25 deg deployable band. This band is the near wall the array stands on. ASSUMPTION.
_comment_geometry: Across the canyon rather than to the horizon: ~4.5 km rim to rim, ~1.5 km deep, tau range in the valley 50 m - 5 km. The far wall subtends roughly +/-20 deg from a detector on the near wall. min_dist is 2 km so the target is the opposite wall rather than the slope underfoot; energy_min/max_pev are deliberately NOT set here, because they would override this window with the tau decay length (147 m - 52 km), which is not the canyon.
_comment_far_wall: The per-role half of the slope criterion. min_slope/max_slope above describe the NEAR wall the array stands on; this describes the FAR wall the tau exits, measured along the arrival azimuth at the point the ray strikes it. Without it the scan asks only that rock is present at the right range, which is true almost everywhere in the Andes. 25 deg is a deliberately permissive floor against Colca's ~40 deg walls -- ASSUMPTION, and the knob most worth checking.
_comment_physics: Particle detection, not radio: no Fresnel clearance, no geomagnetic weighting, and grammage scored as a band because particle content dies after shower maximum whereas radio simply propagates.
_comment_shower_band: = physics.grammage_band_from_energy(3.0, 1000.0, fraction=0.1), i.e. TAMBO's 3 PeV - 1 EeV reach, taken as the depth range where the charged-particle content stays above a tenth of its own maximum. Stated explicitly rather than via energy_min/max_pev only because those also override the distance window. The default (700, 2800) is a GRAND-scale band and rejects every canyon.
_comment_decay: Folded over the spectrum rather than evaluated at one energy. The decay probability runs over three decades across TAMBO's 3 PeV - 1 EeV reach, so a single representative energy chooses the answer rather than approximating it: the sensitivity sweep gave 10878 detector positions at 3 PeV and zero at 100. decay_spectral_index may be a single value to pin the spectrum, or a [low, high] pair to marginalise uniformly over the range when the index is not known -- e.g. [1.5, 2.7]. 2.0 is the canonical slope and is an ASSUMPTION worth the same scrutiny as any other; marginalising costs nothing, since the index integral folds into a weight computed once. shower_development_m is 0 because the grammage band already carries the requirement that enough air was traversed.
_comment_scoring: solid_angle_half_sr defaults to 0.05, a GRAND-scale value. Looking across a canyon the accepted solid angle is 0.2-1.5 sr, so 0.05 saturates the term to ~1 everywhere and it stops discriminating; 0.8 spreads it across the observed range. min_score is the cut that turns the score into an actual filter - with 0.0 the score is computed and then ignored, which is why an earlier run accepted 91.7% of candidates.
_comment_layout: 5000 units at 100 m on a triangular grid. min_width_km is 0 because the array is a strip along a wall, not a blob, and the opening would delete it.
_comment_downsample: 1, not 4: area is measured on the downsampled mask while capacity is measured at full resolution, so a canyon strip only a few pixels wide loses ~30% of its area to downsampling while keeping its detectors. At 1 the two agree. Must match grand_colca_config.json for the masks to combine.
